harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (mariadb-server + galera-4 on Ubuntu 24.04, wsrep_sst_method=rsync). Verified writes from any member replicate to the others, that the cluster stays available with quorum when one member is down and auto-resyncs via IST when it returns, and completed the mandatory sequential-reboot protocol on all three nodes with boot-id proof and post-reboot cluster/data recovery verification.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes (Ubuntu 24.04.3) and cluster host map
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-client, galera-4, rsync on node1/node2/node3
Wrote /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/60-galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address pointing at all 3 IPs, unique wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3 to join (cluster grew 1->2->3, all Synced)
Enabled mariadb systemd service on all three nodes for boot persistence
Created test database/table and verified writes issued on node1, node2, and node3 each replicate to all other members (full mesh)
Stopped mariadb on node3 to simulate member outage; confirmed cluster remained Primary at size 2 and writes on node1/node2 succeeded
Restarted mariadb on node3; confirmed automatic rejoin, IST resync, and receipt of all rows written while it was down
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/data health baseline on all three nodes

Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time, quorum preserved), confirming connection drop, changed boot_id after each reboot, and full Galera cluster/data recovery (size 3, Synced, all rows present) before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: Galera cluster formed across all 3 nodes (Primary component, size 3)
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped size=1, node2 joined size=2, node3 joined size=3; final check confirms all three IPs present and Synced.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member available from the other members
evidence.summary: Inserts issued on node1, node2, and node3 each appear on all other nodes, proving full mesh replication.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available (with quorum) when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: node3 stopped; node1/node2 cluster remained Primary at size 2 and accepted new writes while node3 was down.

evidence.requirement: Automatic resynchronization of a returning member
evidence.summary: node3 restarted and automatically rejoined via IST, reaching Synced state with all rows written during its outage, with no manual intervention.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdd5de93.../Synced/5 rows captured; reboot acknowledged and connection dropped; post-reboot boot_id 1788d797... (changed); mariadb auto-started, rejoined cluster (size 3, Synced), all 5 rows intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 28ae5f98.../Synced/5 rows captured; reboot acknowledged and connection dropped; post-reboot boot_id b3069b40... (changed); mariadb auto-started, rejoined cluster (size 3, Synced), all 5 rows intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfeb3b70.../Synced/5 rows captured; reboot acknowledged and connection dropped; post-reboot boot_id d52d1ebc... (changed); mariadb auto-started, rejoined cluster (size 3, Synced), all 5 rows intact.
